 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents for the injuries sustained by her in the road traffic accident that took place on 26.03.2021.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner as follows:
On 26.03.2021 petitioner along with other inmates was traveling in the bus bearing Reg. No. KA-05-B-6231 and at about 9.15 a.m. near Shettinayakanahalli Cross,
Nadampalli village, middle of Chintamani - Chellur road, Chinthamani Taluk, at that time the driver of the said bus suddenly drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, due to which, back side of tire damaged, caused the accident,
consequent to which petitioner lost balance and hit her leg over the railing and sustained grievous injuries.

It is contended that, immediately after the accident, she shifted to Radhakrishna hospital, Chintamani, and for further treatment she was shifted to Hosmat hospital, Bengaluru wherein she took treatment for the accidental injuries sustained by her.

It is stated that she has spent huge amount for her treatment, medicine etc.,
Nagalakshmi.V vs Ramanjaneya Reddy P.V on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9581846/
2 3.

sentences.text: It is further stated that prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy and was working in drinking water supply and provision shop and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, she is unable to do her work as doing earlier.

It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the bus bearing Reg. No.
KA- 05-B-6231.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
4. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent and hence, he was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 entered appearance through its counsel and filed written statement.
5. The 2nd respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.

It has denied the age,
income and occupation of the petitioner and also the amount spent towards the medical expenses by the petitioner.
It is contended that, owner of the vehicle and the jurisdictional police have not complied Section 134(C)and 158(6) of M.V. Act.
It is further contended that as on the date of accident, the bus not possessed the valid permit and driver did not possess the valid D.L. to drive the same.
It is the contention that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues :-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 26.03.2021 at about 9.15 a.m. when she was proceeding from Chintamani in a bus bearing Reg. No.KA-05-B-6231 as passenger and when reached near Shettinayakanahalli Cross, Nadampalli village, middle of Chintamani - Chellur road, Chinthamani Taluk, at that time driver of the said bus suddenly drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, as a result, back side tire got damaged and the petitioner lost balance and hit her leg over the railing due to which she sustained injuries ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what is the quantum and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
7.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 22 documents as per Ex.P1 to 22.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has examined one witness as RW.1 and and he got marked 4 documents at Ex.R1 to R4.

8. Heard the arguments.
9.

My findings on the above issues as under:-

As per final order For the following:
REASONS 10. Issues No.1:

As per the case of the petitioner, on 26.03.2021 petitioner along with other inmates was travelling in the bus bearing Reg. No. KA-05-B-6231 and at about 9.15 a.m. near Shettinayakanahalli Cross, Nadampalli village, middle of Chintamani - Chellur road, Chinthamani Taluk, at that time the driver of the said bus suddenly drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, due to which, back side of tire damaged, caused the accident, consequent to which petitioner lost balance and hit her leg over the railing and sustained grievous injuries.

The petitioner in order to prove her case, got examined herself as PW.1 and reiterated the averments of the petition and got marked F.I.R, F.I.S, Spot Mahazars, Sketch, IMV report, Wound certificate and Charge Sheet as per Ex.P1 to 7 and P9.
11.

According to the version of petitioner the accident happened near Shettinayakanahalli Cross,
Nadampalli village, middle of Chintamani - Chellur road, Chinthamani Taluk, at that time the driver of the said bus by driving the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner due to which,
back side of tire damaged and caused the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.3 being the Spot Mahazar and Ex.P5 Sketch prepared at the time of mahazar.

On close perusal of the Ex.P3 and Ex.P5 it reflects that petitioner was traveling in the offending bus as a inmate, the driver of the bus drove the same in a negligent manner with high speed, due to which, back side of tire damaged, due to which petitioner sustained injuries.
The said factum is also fortified with the IMV report.
If the driver of bus drove it in a normal speed by observing on moving vehicles on the road, then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Added more the contents of Ex.P.6 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.
Further more, even the chargesheet as per Ex.P9 was also filed as against the driver of the bus.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3, 5 and 6 coupled with Ex.P9 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the bus driver.
12. Even in the instant case the driver of the bus is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part.

After the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending bus bearing registration No.KA- 05-B-6231 concluding that the accident was occurred only due to his negligence.
There is no reason to take a different view.
Therefore, I hold that the accident was occurred only due to the rash and negligent act of driver of the offending bus bearing Reg. No. KA-05-B-6231.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-05-B-6231.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.

14. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
Nagalakshmi.V vs Ramanjaneya Reddy P.V on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9581846/
4

sentences.text:
It is the case of the petitioner that prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy and was working as drinking water supply and provision shop and earning Rs.20,000/-
per month and in order to prove the same, petitioner has produced Form No.3,
Form- A2, Annexure-1, GST certificate, IT returns which shows that the petitioner was running M/s. Sri Chowdeshwari Agri Solutions.
However on perusal of IT returns marked at Ex.P17 reflects that the said income tax was paid for the financial year 2022-23 and the accident was occurred in the year 2021.
Hence the said document is not helpful in the assessment of the income of the deceased.
In the absence of document of income, the tribunal has to consider the notional income of the petitioner.
The incident occurred during the year 2021.
considering the avocation and the year of the accident, I deem it just and proper to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/- per month.
The petitioner claims that she is unable to work due to the injuries sustained to him.
The petitioner got examined the Doctor as PW.2.

In the evidence of doctor, he has deposed that petitioner sustained open type 3 a fracture dislocation left ankle(bimalleolar fracture dislocation), semicircular wound over the aonteromedial aspect of her left ankle, fracture 4th metatarsal fracture left, right leg medial aspect anterior laceration and she underwent external fixation left ankle K-wire fixation left lateral malleolus and left 4 th metatarsal.
On examination he found that the fracture left ankle and 4 th metatarsal has united with residual pain, swelling and stiffness of the left ankle.
Petitioner has developed necrosis i.e. loss of blood supply of the left talus with degenerative changes.
Her left ankle skin graft wounds have healed with disfiguration, itching and numbness.
The healed skin graft irritates her while wearing footwear.
She has a healed donor skin graft on her right thigh.
She has developed a flat deformed foot and has pain on walking short distance and has difficulty in wearing footwear and has deformed left little toe.
He assessed 58% disability to the Left lower limb and 20% whole body disability of the petitioner.
While calculating the loss of future income on account of permanent disability, the functional disability to the whole body has to be considered.
The disability to the whole body shall have to be assessed on the basis of the profession of the injured and relative effect of the disability to his profession.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner are not in dispute and the injuries sustained by him definitely will have an impact on her work.
PW.2 is not a treated doctor and the disability assessed by him has to be taken into consideration carefully.
Hence, considering the nature of the work and impact of disability on his performance, I deem it just and proper to consider 12% disability to her whole body.
It is contended that petitioner was aged 41 years as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred on 26.03.2021.

However, by considering the date of birth Nagalakshmi.V vs Ramanjaneya Reddy P.V on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9581846/
5 mentioned in Ex.P18 Adhaar card as 1981
, the petitioner was aged 40 years at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable to the age of 40 is 15 as per the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation(AIR 2009 SC 3104).

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation(AIR 2009 SC 3104)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.3,24,000/-(Rs.15,000x12x15x12/100)
towards loss of future income on account of permanent disability.

15. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
The wound certificate produced at Ex.P7 shows the injuries sustained by the petitioner due to the accident.

The Ex.P8 Discharge Summary of Hosmat Hospital reveals that petitioner has sustained left ankle bimalleolar fracture dislocation, left foot 4 th MT fracture and left ankle raw area and underwent left ankle spanning exfix application with CRIF of lateral malleolus with k-wire and CRIF of 4th MT with K-wire.
She was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital from 26.03.2021 to 01.04.2021.
Considering these aspects, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.50,000/- towards pain and sufferings.
16. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P10 for Rs.3,04,847/-.
I have examined the medical bills and receipts.

Since the petitioner was treated as inpatient and undergone treatment, there are no reasons to disbelieve the amount spent by the petitioner to the tune of Rs.3,04,847/-, but in the bill No.38 amount paid only Rs.450/- bill has been manipulated as Rs.4,500/-, therefore the said amount has been deducted in the total amount.
The petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,00,347/-.

17. ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD & NOURISHMENT AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
As the petitioner was treated as an inpatient for a period of 7 days, certainly she might have spent amount towards conveyance, attendant charges, nourishing food and other incidental expenses and also at the time of subsequent follow up treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.7,000/- under this head.
18. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of her stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out her avocation for at least 3 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.45,000/- (15,000X3) under this head.

19. LOSS OF AMENITIES IN LIFE/LIFE COMFORTS AND EXPECTANCY OF LIFE/MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS:
Nagalakshmi.V vs Ramanjaneya Reddy P.V on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9581846/
6
The petitioner was aged about 41 years at the time accident and on account of accident, he has to suffer the above disability.
She has to suffer this discomfort and sacrifice the amenities through out her remaining life.
This court has considered disability to the extent of 10% to whole body.
Considering all these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.25,000/- on this head.
20. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:

PW.2 in his evidence has stated that, petitioner will need fusion of the left subtalar joint in future which will cost 1.3 lakhs and she need daily application of vaseline over the skin graft areas which will cost Rs.10,000/-
annually.
There is no estimation is produced.

Hence, by taking into consideration the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by her, I deem it proper to award Rs.25,000/-
under this head.

21. Thus in all, the petitioner entitled for the compensation as here under:
 Sl. Head of  Amount  No. Compensation  1. Loss of future earnings due Rs. 3,24,000.00  to disability  2. Pain and Sufferings Rs. 50,000.00  3.
Medical expenses Rs. 3,00,347.00  4. Conveyance, food and Rs. 7,000.00  nourishment, attendant  charges and other incidental  expenses.
5. Loss of income during laid Rs. 45,000.00  up period 6. Loss of amenities in life/Life Rs. 25,000.00 comforts and expectancy of life 7.
Future medical expenses Rs. 25,000.00 Total Rs. 7,76,347.00
In total, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,76,347/-.
22. Interest:
The petitioner is claiming interest @ 9% p.a. on the compensation amount.

Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding future medical expenses) is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
23. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the bus bearing Reg. No. KA- 05-B-6231.
24.
It is not in dispute that 1st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.

It is the main contention of the respondent No.2 that at the time of accident i.e. on 26.03.2021 offending bus Nagalakshmi.V vs Ramanjaneya Reddy P.V on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9581846/
7 bearing No.KA-05-B-6231 had no valid permit and it expired on 05.01.2017, therefore it is not liable to pay the compensation.
In support of their contention the Respondent No.2 has relied on Ex.R3 which is the history of permit of the vehicle Registration No. KA-05-B-6231.
As per this document the offending bus was having permit for a period from 06.01.2012 to 05.01.2017.
The accident occurred on 26.03.2021.

There is no document to show as on the date of accident the offending bus had valid permit, but 2 nd Respondent has issued the insurance police from 13.09.2020 to 12.09.2021, which makes it clear that the 2 nd Respondent without verifying the permit issued the policy.

At this stage this court has relied on decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court in its judgment between Rani v. National Insurance Company Ltd in Civil Appeal Nos.9078-9079 OF 2017 has held that,
such violation amounts to violation of the policy condition, the insurer has to pay the compensation and recover the same from the insured.

entities.text: Rani v. National Insurance Company Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in its judgment reported in 2023 ACJ 1952 in between G.Shivaputhra vs. P.Shanthamma and another wherein it is held that:
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, section 149 (2)(a)(i)(a) - Motor Insurance - Permit - Liability of insurance company - Pay and recover order- Insurance company examined officer from RTO who deposed that neither the offending autorickshaw was having a permit nor any application to obtain the same was filed - Tribunal exonerated insurance company from liability -

Owner contended that policy was subsequently renewed without verifying whether permit has been obtained which shows that insurance company never intended to dispute its liability on the issue of permit -
Whether non-possession of permit amounts to infraction on the part of owner and tribunal rightly exonerated insurance company from liability -

Held: yes:
however, considering the object of the Act insurance company is directed to pay compensation at the first instance and then recover the amount from owner- insured."

This court has also relied on the decision reported in 2024 ACJ 2304 in between Legal Manager, Shriram General Ins. Co., Ltd. vs. Nagamma and others.
"Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, section 49(2) - Motor Insurance - Permit and fitness certificate - Liability of insurance company - Pay and recover order - Insurance company disputes its liability on the ground that offending canter did not have valid permit and fitness certificate - Driver was prosecuted under section 56 and 66 of M.V. Act and there was a fundamental breach of policy - whether insurance company can be directed to pay compensation and then recover the amount from owner even if there is fundamental breach of policy - Held: yes."
Nagalakshmi.V vs Ramanjaneya Reddy P.V on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9581846/
8

entities.text: Legal Manager, Shriram General Ins. Co., Ltd. vs. Nagamma and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the light of the discussion made supra, the respondent No.2 has successfully established that the offending bus did not possess valid Permit as on the date of accident to ply on the road.

25. Further contention of the respondent No.2 is that the driver of the offending bus has not possessed the valid licence at the time of accident, but they have not produced any document in proof of the same.
Therefore, without production of supportive documents, mere contention does not acceptable.
On perusal of the police documents there is no mention that the driver of the bus not possessed valid driving licence.

26. Now the next question that arises, whether this Tribunal can direct the respondent No.2/Insurance company to pay the award amount together with interest and then recover the same from the insured/respondent No.1.

It is relevant to note that the Doctrine of 'Pay and Recover' was considered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2004) 3 SCC 297 between National Insurance Company V/s Swaran Singh, wherein the liability of the Insurance company was examined in cases of breach of policy condition, the insurer has to indemnify the award amount to the third party and recover the same from the insurer.

entities.text: National Insurance Company V/s Swaran Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence it is clear that the statutory liability is on the Insurance company as per Sec.149 of IMV Act, to pay the compensation first to the claimant and thereafter the insurance company may recover the same from the owner of offending vehicle.

In the recent decision reported in 2018 ACJ 690 (Pappu & others V/s Vinod Kumar Lamba &
another) also the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that the mere fact that the vehicle was duly insured would not perse make the Insurance company liable.

entities.text:
2018 ACJ 690 (Pappu & others V/s Vinod Kumar Lamba &
another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However the Apex Court directed the Insurance Company to pay the compensation amount and recover the same from owner of the vehicle.
This court gave anxious consideration to the principles laid down by the constitutional courts in the above said decision.
In view of the above discussion and the the principles laid down in the above said decisions are squarely applicable to the case on hand.

Therefore following the ratio laid down in the decisions cited supra, this Tribunal intends that it is just and proper to direct the insurer i.e., Respondent No.2 to pay the amount together with interest @ 6% p.a, from the date of claim petition till realization of entire award amount to the petitioner herein.

However the respondent No.2 is at liberty to recover the award amount together with the interest so paid, from the insured/ Respondent No.1, in appropriate execution proceedings as held in Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd V/s Nanjappan & others, reported in (2004) 13 SCC 224.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd V/s Nanjappan & others, reported in (2004) 13 SCC 224
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With this observation, I answered issue No.1 'in the Affirmative' and Issue No.2 'Partly in the affirmative'.

27. Issue No.3: In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,76,347/-(Rupees Seven Lakhs seventy six thousand three hundred and forty seven only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on Rs.7,51,347/- from the date of petition till its realisation.

Nagalakshmi.V vs Ramanjaneya Reddy P.V on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9581846/
9

The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to pay the aforesaid award amount together with interest to the petitioner within 30 days from the date of this order, with liberty to recover the same from the insured/respondent No.1 in appropriate execution proceedings as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd V/s Nanjappan & others reported in (2004) 13 SCC 224.

On deposit of the compensation amount, 60% of the award amount shall be paid to the petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and remaing 40% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 2 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that on 26.03.2021 at about 9.15 a.m. when she was proceeding from Chintamani in a bus bearing Reg. No.KA-05-B-6231 as passenger and when reached near Shettinayakanahalli Cross, Nadampalli village, middle of Chintamani - Chellur road, Chinthamani Taluk, at that time driver of the said bus suddenly drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, as a result, back side tire got damaged and the petitioner lost balance and hit her leg over the railing due to which she sustained injuries ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what is the quantum and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
7.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On close perusal of the Ex.P3 and Ex.P5 it reflects that petitioner was traveling in the offending bus as a inmate, the driver of the bus drove the same in a negligent manner with high speed, due to which, back side of tire damaged, due to which petitioner sustained injuries.
The said factum is also fortified with the IMV report.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3, 5 and 6 coupled with Ex.P9 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the bus driver.
After the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending bus bearing registration No.KA- 05-B-6231 concluding that the accident was occurred only due to his negligence.
He assessed 58% disability to the Left lower limb and 20% whole body disability of the petitioner.
While calculating the loss of future income on account of permanent disability, the functional disability to the whole body has to be considered.
The disability to the whole body shall have to be assessed on the basis of the profession of the injured and relative effect of the disability to his profession.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner are not in dispute and the injuries sustained by him definitely will have an impact on her work.
PW.2 is not a treated doctor and the disability assessed by him has to be taken into consideration carefully.
Hence, considering the nature of the work and impact of disability on his performance, I deem it just and proper to consider 12% disability to her whole body.
, the petitioner was aged 40 years at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable to the age of 40 is 15 as per the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation(AIR 2009 SC 3104).
The accident occurred on 26.03.2021.
There is no document to show as on the date of accident the offending bus had valid permit, but 2 nd Respondent has issued the insurance police from 13.09.2020 to 12.09.2021, which makes it clear that the 2 nd Respondent without verifying the permit issued the policy.
This court has also relied on the decision reported in 2024 ACJ 2304 in between Legal Manager, Shriram General Ins. Co., Ltd. vs. Nagamma and others.
"Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, section 49(2) - Motor Insurance - Permit and fitness certificate - Liability of insurance company - Pay and recover order - Insurance company disputes its liability on the ground that offending canter did not have valid permit and fitness certificate - Driver was prosecuted under section 56 and 66 of M.V. Act and there was a fundamental breach of policy - whether insurance company can be directed to pay compensation and then recover the amount from owner even if there is fundamental breach of policy - Held: yes."
Nagalakshmi.V vs Ramanjaneya Reddy P.V on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9581846/
8
25. Further contention of the respondent No.2 is that the driver of the offending bus has not possessed the valid licence at the time of accident, but they have not produced any document in proof of the same.
On perusal of the police documents there is no mention that the driver of the bus not possessed valid driving licence.
Hence it is clear that the statutory liability is on the Insurance company as per Sec.149 of IMV Act, to pay the compensation first to the claimant and thereafter the insurance company may recover the same from the owner of offending vehicle.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,00,347/-.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.45,000/- (15,000X3) under this head.
Hence, by taking into consideration the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by her, I deem it proper to award Rs.25,000/-
under this head.
21. Thus in all, the petitioner entitled for the compensation as here under:
 Sl. Head of  Amount  No. Compensation  1. Loss of future earnings due Rs. 3,24,000.00  to disability  2. Pain and Sufferings Rs. 50,000.00  3.
However the respondent No.2 is at liberty to recover the award amount together with the interest so paid, from the insured/ Respondent No.1, in appropriate execution proceedings as held in Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd V/s Nanjappan & others, reported in (2004) 13 SCC 224.
27. Issue No.3: In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,76,347/-(Rupees Seven Lakhs seventy six thousand three hundred and forty seven only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on Rs.7,51,347/- from the date of petition till its realisation.
The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to pay the aforesaid award amount together with interest to the petitioner within 30 days from the date of this order, with liberty to recover the same from the insured/respondent No.1 in appropriate execution proceedings as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd V/s Nanjappan & others reported in (2004) 13 SCC 224.
On deposit of the compensation amount, 60% of the award amount shall be paid to the petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and remaing 40% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 2 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
